verified_against_binary: v2.44.5 CORRECTS PUBLISHED COUNTS in env.CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT -- and its own first draft got one of them wrong in the same way it was documenting. True values: asar 1.40609.0 = 9 (ASCII 9 + UTF-16LE 0); CLI 2.1.250 = 59 (ASCII 56 + UTF-16LE 3). THREE instruments, three distinct failures. (a) grep -c counts LINES, and an asar or Bun binary is effectively ONE line, so it under-reported the asar as 3 -- a real error, that correction stands. (b) An ASCII-only raw-byte regex CANNOT SEE UTF-16LE-stored strings; it under-reported the CLI as 56, and the draft published that as 'byte-level truth'. (c) A null-stripped extract does NOT fabricate matches -- it DECODES UTF-16LE (ASCII char + \x00), which is exactly why it returned 59: 56 ASCII + 3 UTF-16 = 59. The originally published 59 was correct, and the draft's stated mechanism ('joins non-contiguous fragments') was invented to explain a discrepancy rather than tested -- the very failure the same release documents. Rule: COUNT IN BOTH ENCODINGS or say which one you counted; an ASCII count is never 'byte-level truth'. The conclusion is unaffected and still rests on all nine asar occurrences, including the newly-read RESERVED-NAME GUARD (a plugin's declared env may not redefine the token). Shipped scripts audited and clean. Credit: the UTF-16 blind spot was found by the cowork-harness session auditing its own instruments after reading this repo's counting-failure writeup. No baseline moves. v2.44.4 WITHDRAWS A SENTENCE OF OUR OWN that misled a skill author, and records two dead ends so the next reader does not re-derive them. (1) The Cowork architecture state page said 'the host-path strings visible in /proc/mounts are not usable VM paths' -- which reads as HOST PATHS ARE PRESENT BUT USELESS, and was taken as licence to build a mount-table lookup (prefix-match the file-tool path against a mount's host side, rewrite to the VM side) that would have replaced the whole discovery ladder. The only verbatim mount line on record shows the mount SOURCE is /proc/self/fd/3 -- a fuse descriptor, not a host path -- so there is NO host->VM mapping in the table and nothing to prefix-match. Sentence withdrawn; the finding is now stated where the mount model is described rather than buried in a line captured to prove that delete-approval involves no remount. OPEN and flagged as such: one line captured for another purpose is thin evidence about a whole table, and no full /proc/mounts dump from a live host-loop session has been read here. (2) NEW registry entry env.CLAUDE_CODE_INVOKED_SKILLS -- declared but unconsumed in 2.1.250: three occurrences, no writer and no reader (string table; the static key list feeding spawnEnvKeys(), which builds a set of key NAMES and assigns nothing; and a const whose sole occurrence is its own declaration). It is the obvious name to reach for when asking whether a shell can learn which skill or plugin is executing, and the answer is NO -- ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} is likewise a substitution token into skill DEFINITION text, not an env var, which is where the 'Base directory for this skill:' prefix comes from. Identity travels via the model passing what it already knows. (3) The 522-directory session tree gains the guidance an author needs and would not guess: hundreds of directories, growing, almost all permission-denied from inside any one session -- yet CHEAP to search, because refusal happens at the DIRECTORY level (drwxr-x--- owned by nobody:nogroup, no group overlap), so a walker is turned away per sibling rather than descending. That same property scopes such a search to your own session with no filter you have to write, which is a second argument against the mount-table lookup, since a table read sees every slug's mounts. ccinternals.dev: NO CHANGE NEEDED and verified rather than assumed -- shell.runs-as-its-own-user already publishes the 522 shape correctly ('visible by name but their contents are refused... holds hundreds of entries', with a caveat that listings show scale not concurrency), and no published fact touches the mount table, host paths, or an env identity channel. Bounds for file 36 re-derived again. No baseline moves. v2.44.3 CORRECTS A MOUNT-SHAPE OVERGENERALISATION and records the FIRST live inside-session confirmation of the Cowork mount model. Ch36/L140's table and the cowork-architecture state page both asserted .local-plugins/cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version> as THE shape, labelled 'version-pinned'. It is one instance: the Desktop builds that tail as guestCompatibleRelative(accountOrgRoot, installPath), a MIRROR of the host install layout with no fixed depth. v2.44.1 corrected the underlying claim in the registry from the Desktop builder but left both prose copies stale -- the partial-fix pattern where the record you are looking at gets corrected and its copies do not. A live counterexample from a cowork-harness container-fidelity run makes it concrete: .local-plugins/marketplaces/local-desktop-app-uploads/<plugin> -- three segments, 'marketplaces' not 'cache', no version, NO PLUGIN ID, so an id-keyed join cannot fire on it. The sibling .remote-plugins/plugin_<id> is different in kind and safe: the id IS the leaf, one directory per id by construction. FIRST LIVE CONFIRMATION: every Cowork mount claim in this skill was previously read from app.asar or the guest disk image; a real host-loop session (relayed by the creative-problem-solving project) confirms four at once from inside a running shell -- the .remote-plugins/plugin_<id> shape, $HOME = the session root (Ch37/L146, previously probe-only), the adjective-adjective-noun slug format (Ch31/L117), and the namespace split itself, with the plugin id BYTE-IDENTICAL in the host and VM paths (which is what makes a basename join work where a path cannot). Also recorded: ~/.claude/plugins does not exist in the VM, so a search rooted there is inert. METHOD NOTE from the same transcript: it reported an upward directory walk as 'what found' the scripts; it was not -- the agent had seeded the walk with a /sessions path learned from an earlier find, not the file-tool path the instruction named. A trace showing the right answer does not establish the mechanism that produced it. ccinternals.dev: plugins.plugin-root-per-consumer sharpened -- token substitution happens in files the RUNTIME LOADS as definitions (skill body, command, hook), NOT in a file your skill READS at run time, where the token arrives literally and names nothing; and the token is absent from the shell environment, so referring to it in a command yields an empty string rather than an error. That distinction is what cost a real skill a silent fallback to a degraded path. plugins.plugin-files-are-mounted needed no change -- it already said discover at runtime. Bounds for file 36 re-derived (which also fixed a pre-existing off-by-one on L138). No baseline moves. v2.44.2 is TOOLING, not new binary findings: it turns two conventions that were being held by memory into checks, after both failed inside a single release. (1) NEW scripts/check-json-format.js pins each index JSON's exact on-disk serialization (indent + trailing newline + KEY ORDER), wired into both CI workflows, with 6 tests including controls that must trip. The index files do not share a format -- cross-references.json and troubleshooting.json are indent=1, topic-index.json / registry.json / author-facts.json are indent=2 with a trailing newline, and the generated semantic-index.json is indent=2 with NO trailing newline -- and rewriting one at the wrong indent buries the real change under a five-figure diff. That happened twice in v2.44.0/v2.44.1 despite a CLAUDE.md warning, which is the argument for a check over a convention. THE NON-OBVIOUS FINDING that made the checker non-trivial: JavaScript objects do not preserve the order of INTEGER-LIKE keys -- "129", "31999", "2307090146" are array indices to the engine, so JSON.parse+JSON.stringify silently hoists every numeric key to the front in ascending order. cross-references.json is keyed by lesson id and topic-index.json's keyword_map holds gate ids, so ANY Node read/rewrite of those two reorders thousands of lines while changing nothing; Python preserves insertion order and does not. The checker therefore ships its own ~60-line order-preserving parser rather than comparing against JSON.stringify -- a checker built on the round-trip it polices would have had to declare those two files permanently broken or accept the reordering it exists to catch. (2) state.js --audit now distinguishes AHEAD of baseline from BEHIND it. It compared as_of by string inequality, so a record verified against a NEWER artifact than the baseline printed as 'behind baseline' -- and the only way to keep the gate green was to restamp a newer verification as older than it was, which v2.44.1 did to two entries. Version comparison is now numeric (a malformed version sorts as BEHIND so a typo still fails), behind exits 1 (it exited 0 before, leaving the gate resting entirely on a grep), ahead is reported and does not fail, and the two CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/CLAUDE_EFFORT entries carry their honest 2.1.250 stamps. No lesson content changed; no baseline moves. v2.44.1 CORRECTS TWO SHIPPED CLAIMS about env vars, both surfaced while answering an external plugin author and both re-derived first-party (CLI 2.1.233/2.1.246/2.1.247/2.1.248/2.1.250 + Desktop app.asar 1.37937.3, newer than the 1.30096.1 baseline; baseline deliberately NOT moved). (1) Ch17/L90 was headed 'CLAUDE_EFFORT -- a skill frontmatter field, NOT an env var'. WRONG, and instructively so: the evidence behind it was real -- there is genuinely NO read site (process.env/a./env. forms all ZERO in 2.1.250) -- but an env var has TWO directions and only the inbound one was checked. Outbound it is unambiguous: the Bash/hook child env builder Fke() sets t.CLAUDE_EFFORT=e.effortLevel, the name sits in the spawn-env key list beside CLAUDECODE/CLAUDE_PID/TRACEPARENT, and the CLI's OWN hook-input schema says 'Also exposed to hook commands and Bash as the CLAUDE_EFFORT env var.' Precise statement: WRITE-ONLY -- exported to children, never consumed. Ch24/L107's 'CLAUDE_EFFORT-as-env is a no-op' STANDS (setting it inbound does nothing), as do the frontmatter field and the ${CLAUDE_EFFORT} template token. Present in every binary on disk back to 2.1.233; v2.1.120 is long gone from disk so whether L90 was wrong when written or drifted later is UNRESOLVED -- corrected, not back-dated. (2) registry env.CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT conflated a SUBSTITUTION TOKEN with an ENV VAR, and its note that 'bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/x.sh works under VM-loop' was read -- by this skill's own maintainer -- as meaning a model-issued Bash call can read $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT. It cannot, on any surface checked. The token is text-substituted into plugin-declared definition strings; the env var reaches only THREE child spawns (plugin commands, MCP stdio servers, MCP headersHelper). The Bash child env DOES inherit the process env, so the var would pass through if it were set there -- it is not. Desktop 1.37937.3: all three occurrences are substitution sites, none an env assignment. Entry now separates (A) substitution from (B) outbound env, and adds re-derived VM mount shapes: remote => /sessions/<id>/mnt/.remote-plugins/<plugin id> (tail is exactly the id, which is what lets a file-tool path basename join the two namespaces); local => .local-plugins/<guestCompatibleRelative(accountOrgRoot, installPath)> -- a relative-path MIRROR of the host layout, NOT a fixed cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version> depth; plus the TRAP that skills are separately advertised at /sessions/<id>/mnt/.claude/<...>/<sanitizeSkillName(name)>, a SKILL mount containing no plugin scripts/, so a name-matched search can SUCCEED and still be wrong -- match a sentinel file, never a directory name. New registry entry env.CLAUDE_EFFORT; ipc.LocalSessions_reasoningConfig sharpened to say INBOUND no-op. Both entries' as_of stay at the 2.1.231 baseline per this registry's convention (as_of is a reconciliation stamp; the artifacts actually read are named in the summary). METHOD LESSON, recorded in the lesson itself: confirming how a symbol is NOT used does not establish that it is unused, and 'is X an env var' is two questions. Both errors were caught by an external reader asking which field a claim came from, not by this repo's own checks. v2.44.0 EXTENDS Ch45/L167 against the standalone CLI 2.1.248 + 2.1.250 and a corpus of 269 real re-attachment records, and CORRECTS a claim this session's own author made mid-investigation. (1) THE TOKEN ESTIMATOR IS RESOLVED and the lesson's 'deliberately not claimed' section closes: Math.round(chars/4), identical in 2.1.246/2.1.248/2.1.250 -- so the 'token' gate is exactly a CHARACTER gate with zero conversion error (truncates at 20,002 chars, last safe 20,001, survivor always exactly 20,000). The widely-repeated claim that a char-based lint overstates overage because prose runs above 4 chars/token is WRONG, because nothing in this path ever counts tokens. Method: export-uniqueness resolved it at 2.1.248/2.1.250 but returned ZERO at 2.1.246 -- an artifact of the instrument, not the build, since 2.1.246 predates Ch43/L162's chunk consolidation and uses mangled cross-chunk aliases. The technique that works in BOTH layouts is to read the consuming chunk's own import statement and follow the alias through the exporting chunk's export block; a bare-name export grep silently false-negatives on an alias-mangled bundle (same family as the hidden-dot-dir and gzip-fcache traps). (2) RECOVERY CHANNEL CORRECTED. The `path` field reaching the model is `${source}:${name}` -- a source-qualified identifier, never a file location (269 records, all identifiers; source is a closed enum). An earlier pass concluded from this that the marker's 'use Read on the skill path' was unexecutable and RELAYED that to a peer project before checking it. It is wrong: the loader prepends `Base directory for this skill: <absolute dir>` to the stored CONTENT, and truncation is head-preserving, so that line survives by construction -- 586/651 entries and 99/101 TRUNCATED entries carry it. The residual, and the only operational part, is the exception: recovery depends on whether the base directory STILL EXISTS WHEN THE LINE IS READ -- a property of when you look, not of the skill. Three states: (a) no directory at all (single-file commands/*.md, some builtins) -- cannot fire, but nothing misleads; (b) directory still present -- works; (c) directory died since -- LOOKS EXECUTABLE AND FAILS, worse than having none. MEASURED over 56 distinct base dirs in the corpus: 49 DEAD, of which 46 are version-stamped plugin-cache paths removed by an ordinary upgrade (superpowers/6.1.1 dead with 6.3.0 present; skill-creator-plus/0.4.2 dead with 0.9.0/0.10.0 present); bundled skills reach the same state via join(tmpdir(),'bundled-skills',VERSION,randomBytes(16).hex), random per run, whose recorded root is entirely gone. Every dead path was alive when written and resolves inside a live run, so this is NOT 'recovery is broken'; the reachable failure is RESUME AFTER UPGRADE (transcript replay re-registers stored content verbatim), flagged as INFERENCE -- path-death measured, failing Read not observed. Three framings of this section shipped in one release: the first checked the wrong field, the second generalised from the `bundled:` prefix, both refuted by a peer project's checks. Why three bundled skills carry no base dir while bundled:verify does is left unexplained rather than tidied. Lesson recorded: verifying that one channel does not carry a thing is not evidence that no channel does. (3) THE THREE UNEXPLAINED CONSTANTS are the post-compaction FILE RESTORE, assembled by the same function: five slots, a per-file 5,000-token cap, a 50,000 combined cap, over a per-tool-use-context LRU of 5,000 entries / 26,214,400 bytes. 'The five most recently read files' is wrong as a summary -- the slice runs LAST, after excluding memory files, the agent's plan file, files whose Read survives in retained messages, and (only on the partial-compaction caller) pinned memory-dir entries, so MICROCOMPACTION RESTORES A DIFFERENT FILE SET than full compaction. This qualifies rather than overturns the references exemption: reference files stay exempt from both SKILL caps but are candidates for this budget. Per-agent scoping is stated as a property of TODAY'S CALLERS, not the mechanism (the dispatch reads an override slot that would pass a shared cache through), and an SDK-layer merge was NOT traced, so no 'only' is claimed. (4) THREE CHUNK-LOCAL CALLERS, one of them partial/microcompaction -- so a survey counting only full-compaction boundaries undercounts exposure; whole-binary greps for the assembler's name also hit unrelated homonyms. (5) FIRST EMPIRICAL CORPUS for this lesson: 269 records / 651 entries / 101 truncated, every truncated one exactly 20,000 chars, up to 7 co-invoked skills, combined never observed above 17,207 -- so six- and seven-skill co-invocation is ORDINARY and the combined cap is protected by typical skills being small, not by rarity. A first pass reported 271: that count came from grepping a distinctive string across a directory tree and swept in a peer project's notes and a stored tool-result dump. A corpus-wide grep for a distinctive string sweeps the artifacts of everyone investigating that string, including yourself -- and this lesson is now itself such an artifact. (6) PIN-VALUES TABLE gains 2.1.248/2.1.250 rows, where `_On` is the COMBINED 25,000 cap at 2.1.248 and the PER-SKILL 5,000 cap at 2.1.250 -- one release apart, so a note pinned to that symbol is not merely stale, it is INVERTED. Artifact-class note added: earlier rows are the Desktop-managed host agent, the new ones the standalone CLI (symbols verified to match at 2.1.246). Chapter 45 retitled to cover both post-compaction budgets. DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED: ccinternals.dev. Its published advice ('the file on disk is untouched, so re-reading the skill from its path recovers the full text') is TRUE and actionable; the correction above is a lesson-layer implementation detail an author cannot act on, and publishing it would have introduced a false obstacle to the one recovery path the page recommends. No baseline moves: CLI content baseline stays 2.1.231, Desktop 1.30096.1. troubleshooting.json and cross-references.json gain their first L167 entries (both had zero). v2.43.9 carries v2.43.8's two findings into the PUBLISHED author layer, which v2.43.8 changed only the lesson for. The page already advised 'push detail into reference files' -- now verified correct about the budget, but it did not state what the move TRADES: the shortened skill body tells the reader it was cut, while material that came from a reference and later falls out of the conversation leaves NO such signal, so the pointer to those references must survive near the top and is doing MORE work after the move than before it. Also added as a reassurance, so authors do not defend against the wrong thing: the shared limit is counted per agent, so dispatching to sub-agents does not consume the main thread's budget. Both are phrased without naming tools, versions or exact figures, per the layer's discipline. Method note for this pass: the gap was found by grepping the published fact for the asymmetry and getting a FALSE POSITIVE -- the phrase 'no marker' was present, but from the unrelated truncation-vs-zeroing text added in 2.43.7. A keyword hit is not a coverage check; read the sentence it landed in. v2.43.8 RESOLVES the one open question in L167 and adds a fact nobody had. N3n was an unresolved cross-chunk import; chasing the alias chain (cqd as N3n, Ox as cqd) gives `function Ox(e){let t=e??null,o=new Map;for(let[r,s] of n().invokedSkills.skills()) if(s.agentId===t) o.set(r,s); return o}`. (1) REFERENCE FILES ARE EXEMPT, verified: the map comes from a dedicated invokedSkills REGISTRY populated by invoking a skill -- it never scans messages and never inspects tool results, so a references/*.md pulled in with Read is a plain tool result this budget does not see. Moving prose into a reference genuinely removes it from BOTH caps and it does not reappear later. Caveat retained: reference content still lives in ordinary context and is compacted with NO marker, whereas the skill body announces its own truncation. (2) THE BUDGET IS PER AGENT, not per session -- the map is filtered by s.agentId===t (null = main thread), so a sub-agent's invoked skills are budgeted separately and a fan-out does not spend the main thread's 25,000 tokens; siblings Fx/Ex prune the registry per agent on exit. (3) Corrects this lesson's own earlier misreading: N3n(e) takes an agentId, NOT a message list -- nothing walks the transcript. v2.43.7 makes L167 and its published author-fact PRECISE about a distinction both described as 'silent': only ONE of the two compaction failures is observable by the model, and it decides what recovery advice can work. Per-skill TRUNCATION is observable -- oXo returns slice+marker and that value is what is pushed into the invoked_skills attachment (o.push({...,content:u})), so the marker is IN-BAND and its own text tells the reader to Read the skill path for the full text. Combined-cap ZEROING is NOT observable -- the over-budget branch `continue`s before the push, so the skill is absent from the attachment with no marker and no entry, and a model has no baseline to notice an absence against; `if(o.length===0) return null` means a total drop produces no block at all. Consequence for authors, now stated in both layers: a recovery instruction of the form 'if a later section appears missing, say so and re-read from disk' is SOUND for truncation and CANNOT FIRE for zeroing -- write it, but do not let it read as covering both, or it becomes apparent coverage over a silent failure, which is the failure it was meant to prevent. Prompted by the creative-problem-solving session asking whether the precondition held BEFORE building on it. v2.43.6 adds a cross-cutting ADDENDUM to Ch44/L166 naming the class behind four wrong answers this chapter produced in one day: a raw non-ASCII grep across a \uXXXX re-encoding; a length computed after re.sub(r'[^\x20-\x7e]','') deleted the newlines being counted; the same wrong length reached INDEPENDENTLY by another party via grep -o anchored on '[', which cannot return a leading newline; and 'no such runtime is known' when the counterexample sat two lessons below in the same file. NONE was a reasoning error -- each was a SEARCH STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE OF RETURNING THE DISCONFIRMING CASE, returning a confident plausible result. Two agreed, which is why L167's 'agreement between derived sources is not corroboration' is not a caution about carelessness: searches sharing a blind spot converge on the same wrong answer RELIABLY, and convergence reads as confirmation. The check that would have caught all four is one question asked before believing any negative: WHAT COULD THIS SEARCH HAVE RETURNED? -- not 'did I search carefully', since all four were careful. Two corollaries: 'none is known' is a claim about the search, not the world, so a risk statement naming an unknown FUTURE counterexample is a prompt to hunt a PRESENT one in material already held; and a small plausible correction deserves more suspicion than a large implausible one (both marker measurements landed 2 chars from the established figure, which reads as refinement). Generalises to any absence claim -- a tool not in a list, a string not in a bundle, a gate not in an fcache. Ch37/L129's system/init-is-authoritative rule is the positive form: prefer the record that ENUMERATES over the reconstruction that INFERS, because an enumeration can be checked for completeness and an inference cannot. Formulation contributed by the skill-creator-plus session. v2.43.5 WITHDRAWS the one-line probe published in v2.43.3's L164 addendum. `BASE="$([ -d mnt/outputs ] && echo mnt/outputs || echo outputs)"` reintroduces the doubling bug on CHAT MODE, silently: there the shell already starts INSIDE the outputs dir, so the test finds no nested mnt/outputs and the fallback appends outputs/ -> <outputs>/outputs/. The refutation was ALREADY IN THE SAME CHAPTER -- L166's surface table, two lessons below. Root cause: one bit of evidence, three-plus surfaces; the probe tested for the Cowork mount and assumed everything else was CLI-shaped. Caught by the skill-creator-plus session. The PRINCIPLE survives (capability over identity; runtime discrimination, not host-path derivation); the implementation does not. Better default now recorded: a script should NOT self-locate -- the CALLER holds the file tools, has resolved the workspace, and is the only party that can name a user-visible path, so it passes an absolute destination to every shell command and dispatch, and the script echoes back what it actually wrote. Standalone scripts take the destination as a REQUIRED ARGUMENT and fail loudly rather than inventing a directory. A sentinel-anchor probe (write a marker with a FILE TOOL, then locate it from the shell) is recorded as an UNTESTED sketch only. (1) change.your-own-skill-can-be-cut, on the page 'What can change without any version bump?' because that is exactly what compaction does to an author's own text mid-session: the per-skill cut keeps ~20k chars and is WRITTEN BACK so a later compaction cannot recover the tail, while the shared cross-skill budget EMPTIES a skill outright and it stays gone for the session; packed most-recently-used first at already-shortened sizes, so the skill that vanishes is usually not the largest. Numbers are deliberately given as an order of magnitude with the exactness in a caveat -- the behaviours are durable, the constants are a release away from changing. (2) delivery.no-local-server, on 'Why did my skill's output never reach the user?': serving a file and opening a browser at it does not work, and the reasoning is phrased as the CONSTRAINT (what your shell starts runs where the shell runs; a file path is not reachable that way) rather than the capability ('there is no browser'), so it stays true whether or not the in-app browser gates are on for a given account -- wording converged on with the skill-creator-plus session. Both facts avoid naming tools or versions, per the layer's own discipline. v2.43.3 extends Ch44/L164 with a THIRD correct path form and the principle that follows from it, prompted by a downstream skill scoping a fix around 'host detection' that turned out to be unnecessary. L164's table gave bash only the ABSOLUTE /sessions/<id>/mnt/outputs/ form (what the tool description advises); a RELATIVE mnt/outputs/... is equally correct and contains NO session id, because bash's cwd is deterministically the session root and mnt/ sits directly in it (first-party: a real session's bash `ls -a .` lists mnt, and a relative bash write lands in the session root -- the same mechanism that produces the scratchpad failure). That reduces the two-forms rule to TWO CONSTANT PREFIXES per runtime (CLI: outputs/ + outputs/; Cowork host-loop: bare + mnt/outputs/), so a cross-surface skill needs RUNTIME DISCRIMINATION, NOT HOST-PATH DERIVATION -- it never needs /Users/.../local_<id>, the session id, or CLAUDE_CODE_* markers. The shell can discriminate itself with one fail-safe existence test ([ -d mnt/outputs ]) and should PRINT the branch it took, which converts this chapter's defining silent-failure property into a visible one. The wrong value was also plausible -- off by exactly 2 from the established figure, which reads as a satisfying small correction rather than a red flag.
